profiles.summary: The endpoint still answers tempo/v1.19.1-a9d6748 (block 50,959,588 on 2026-11-26) and no later tag exists. tempo main now pins evm2 7c9f3b6d instead of 35aa3280 and reth 5537d69 instead of 167933d, so the next release will carry them. The 14 evm2 instruction and jump analysis files are byte identical between the two evm2 commits; the changed files touch EIP-7702 caller checks, the per frame memory limit, MODEXP with a missing modulus and block access list code hashes. All reruns match, and the long stateful sequences of cycle 26 now give word level matches on Tempo.

deltas.delta: tempo main's Cargo.lock pins evm2 7c9f3b6deb23005fc84596ba1b13a6492d942014 (was 35aa3280 in a9d6748 and in cycle 25's copy of main), reth 5537d6927c14d0be2d3b1505fd305097014233d0 (was 167933d) and reth-core 15c627da; ruint 1.21.1, alloy-primitives 1.7.3, fixed-cache 0.1.10 and keccak-asm 0.1.9 are unchanged. No tempo tag after v1.19.1 exists (v1.19.2, v1.20.0 and their rc tags return 404), so the endpoint still runs 35aa3280.

A crawl of the evm2 crate module tree at both commits (137 and 138 files) shows 14 changed files and 1 new test file. interpreter/instructions/{arithmetic,bitwise,control,crypto,host,i256,memory,stack,system}.rs, bytecode/analysis.rs, bytecode/analysis/x86.rs and bytecode/analysis/aarch64.rs are byte identical. Changed: version/mod.rs (default memory limit per frame from 2^32-1 bytes to 100 MiB), precompiles/modexp.rs (an input that ends before the modulus returns mod_len zero bytes without padding), ethereum/mod.rs (EIP-3607 exempts a delegation designator only when EIP7702 is enabled), evm/bal/changes.rs (a block access list code change seeds the bytecode hash from CodeChange::code_hash), evm/mod.rs, evm/system.rs, evm/inspector.rs, evm/precompile.rs (inspector and refund bookkeeping), evm/state/mod.rs (log buffer reuse), bytecode/mod.rs and precompiles/kzg and bn254 (tests).

The release workflow on main still builds x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu and aarch64-apple-darwin with features asm-keccak,jemalloc,otlp and without the jit feature (release.yml lines 131-138); bin/tempo keeps keccak-cache-global in its default features (Cargo.toml line 155).

Under TIP-1060 Refund mode, the default, every zero to nonzero SSTORE pays the 245,000 gas creditable portion upfront whatever the slot's transaction-original value, and the refund is settled only after the top-level frame returns. A dirty recreation X to 0 to Y inside one transaction, which costs about 100 gas on Ethereum under EIP-2200, costs 245,000 gas of gross budget on Tempo. debug_traceCall showed one 16-pool swap round using 12.8 million gross gas in its frame against 7.05 million net for the call.

cleared.result: Every returned word equals the reference interpreter: a64 128 words in one call (5.19 million gas), a512 1,024 words in one call (16.59 million gas), b in three calls, c and c2 32 words each, d300 27 words in one frame (9.17 million gas, original cycle 26 driver, ERC-6909 balance slots at mapping slot 4 and the driver's output slots pre-set to 1, which the reference shows changes no word). e gives the same ten words on Tempo, on both Arc endpoints and on Ethereum (reth): the second CREATE2 returns address 0, the old code still runs (mark 0xA) and the code hash is unchanged. The cycle 26 failures were gas: Tempo caps the gas of an eth_call (the verifier measured the cap at 50,000,000; this unit recorded 25,000,000), TIP-1060 Refund mode charges 245,000 gas upfront for every zero to nonzero write including the driver's recreated output slots, and a CREATE2 address collision consumes the gas passed to it, leaving the step 1/64 of its budget. The driver used for a, b, c, c2 and e (src/Seq27.sol) keeps outputs in transient storage and bounds the second CREATE2 to 2,000,000 gas; what it asks of the PoolManager is unchanged. The FullMath.mulDiv (src/libraries/FullMath.sol:14) and mulDivRoundingUp (line 109) calls of SqrtPriceMath (src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol:31, 86, 188, 234) and SwapMath.computeSwapStep (src/libraries/SwapMath.sol:51) in those rounds, and the transient delta accounting (src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:21-39, NonzeroDeltaCount.sol:14-32), compute the same values as the specification.

cleared.check: evm2 7c9f3b6d, which tempo main pins for the next release: do any of its changes alter the opcodes the PoolManager uses or the jump destination analysis?
cleared.result: No. The arithmetic, bitwise, control, crypto, host, i256, memory, stack and system instruction files and the three analysis files are byte identical to 35aa3280. The new 100 MiB per frame memory limit cannot be reached with gas: 3,276,800 words of memory cost about 2.1 times 10^10 gas against a 500,000,000 block gas limit, and the PoolManager's frames use kilobytes. The EIP-3607 change concerns transaction senders with delegation code, not contract calls. The PoolManager makes no MODEXP call. The verifier found crates/evm2/src/interpreter/memory.rs byte-identical at both commits, so the new per-frame limit lives in another file than the one cited.

cleared.check: Does the reth commit tempo main pins for the next release (5537d69) commit speculative prewarm results without re-running a transaction?
cleared.result: No. Reuse still needs prewarm_reuse (default false), no decoded block access list, and reuses_prewarm_results from the EVM config (default false, not overridden by tempo main), so settle (src/PoolManager.sol:349-364) always measures a balance on state the validator executed.

cleared.check: TIP-1060 Refund mode charges 245,000 gas upfront for every zero to nonzero write in a transaction, including slots cleared earlier in the same transaction, and refunds only after the top-level frame. Can an ordinary account use this to make other users' PoolManager calls fail?
cleared.result: No loss or freeze path. The PoolManager forwards all remaining gas to hooks and native recipients (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:134, src/types/Currency.sol:48) and never caps a sub-call, so the charge only raises the gas limit a user's own transaction must carry. The writes that can go from zero to nonzero in a swap (feeGrowthGlobal at src/libraries/Pool.sol:446-448, tick crossings at Pool.sol:602, liquidity at Pool.sol:427) are the ones F-064 already prices at TIP-1000 rates; ERC-6909 balances (src/ERC6909.sol:17, PoolManager.sol:322-336) are the caller's own. A withdrawal clears slots and mints credits rather than creating them.

cleared.check: L-1071 for Arc: cache library and key of the execution cache and precompile cache in reth v2.2.0 (88505c7f), which arc-node main pins for reth-engine-tree and reth-execution-cache.
cleared.result: The execution cache (crates/engine/execution-cache/src/cached_state.rs lines 84 and 669-675) uses fixed-cache 0.1.8 with keys B256 code hash, (Address, StorageKey) and Address; fixed-cache's get compares the stored key with key.equivalent before returning a value (src/lib.rs lines 314-339), so a hash collision returns a miss, not another slot's value. The precompile cache (crates/engine/tree/src/tree/precompile_cache.rs lines 44 and 184-186) is a moka cache per precompile address keyed by the whole input bytes plus the spec, and caches only successful outputs. The fixed-cache crate checksum c41c7aa6 matches arc-node's lock. Arc's endpoints run unpublished commits, so this reads the closest published source.

leadResults.answer: All match. With the setup storage computed in the reference interpreter and passed as stateDiff, a64 ran its four rounds in one eth_call (128 words) and a512 its 32 rounds in one call (1,024 words); b's reverted unlock between two identical swaps ran in one call; c, c2 and d300 (27 words, 300 currencies in one frame) matched; e gave the same ten words as Ethereum and both Arc endpoints. a64, a512, c, c2 and e also match under T14 rules. The cycle 26 failures came from Tempo's eth_call gas cap (50,000,000 as the verifier measured it; recorded here as 25,000,000), TIP-1060's 245,000 gas upfront charge on every zero to nonzero write (the driver's output array is cleared and recreated each step) and the all-gas cost of a CREATE2 collision, not from the interpreter.
